knownCaveats.title: KG4E-DISC-01: a volatility set of literal VALUES cannot generalise

knownCaveats.title: KG5A-DISC-01: the governed release cannot be built from the production corpus
knownCaveats.detail: finalize-regulatory-release.ts selects FROM standards_master with no WHERE clause, so release membership is the whole table. Production holds 2,390 full-text rows with source_key NULL on all of them, so Axis B of the approval contract is unsatisfiable from them and 0 of 35 governed citations reconcile as identical (18 content-differ, 17 missing). Measured on disposable copies of the real production corpus: seed:safescope-standards rewrote standard_text and title on five live rows (1910.146, 1910.219, 1910.36, 30 CFR 56.12016, 30 CFR 56.14105) and then crashed on a unique-index collision, because stage 1 inserts 29 CFR 1910.147 while stage 2 tries to rename the pre-existing bare 1910.147 to the same string. Not idempotent, not transactional, left the corpus at 2,396 rows with a duplicate citation pair. On a clean corpus the same seed is idempotent and correctly refuses to re-finalize an active release, so the defect is specific to a non-empty differently-formatted corpus -- which is exactly production.

knownCaveats.title: 15 CONTENT_DIFFERENCE/BLOCKING shadow comparisons against production's real corpus
knownCaveats.detail: With the release active on a production-shaped corpus, the resolver is healthy on all 35 citations (RESOLVER_FAILURE 35 -> 0) and 27 resolve APPROVED_EXACT -- but 15 of those 27 classify CONTENT_DIFFERENCE and therefore BLOCKING, because production carries the full eCFR section dump (56,026 bytes for 1910.1200) where the governed record carries the reviewed 1,141-byte clause-accurate artifact. This is NOT a release defect: every BLOCKING record resolved with resolverHealth OK and governedBackingState APPROVED_EXACT, every digest reproduces, and the corpus is byte-identical. KG-5A's 'release active' column showed EXACT_MATCH on all 35 only because it ran on a corpus that had been REPLACED by the governed rows -- the step KG-5A then proved unsafe. Cross-checked two independent ways: KG-5A's reconciliation found 18 PRODUCTION_ROW_CONTENT_DIFFERS, of which 3 are NEW_REVIEW_REQUIRED and never reach a content comparison; 18 - 3 = 15. BLOCKING means 'would put a materially wrong claim in front of a customer IF GOVERNED MODE WERE ENABLED' -- it does not block SHADOW, which is customer-invisible, and it does not block activation with the cutover variables absent.
knownCaveats.whyNotYetAuthoritative: The KG-5B SHADOW comparison selected its legacy input with the repository's prefix-insensitive matcher (normalizeCitationForMatch), NOT by exercising the live hydrateStandardReferences customer path. 15 is therefore a corroborated DISCOVERY count, not an authoritative customer-path equivalence result. The difference may represent a true regulatory content difference, a storage/citation granularity difference, the governed artifact being an exact subsection of a larger legacy section dump, a normalization-only difference, a resolver pairing difference, or another evidence-backed classification. It must not be prejudged.
knownCaveats.resolution: KG-5C re-measured all 15 through the REAL customer path on both body-text tiers. The KG-5B PAIRING was correct and the count of 15 is confirmed -- what was too coarse was the classification. All 15 classify GOVERNED_REVIEWED_RENDERING on Path A and Path B: the delivered text is byte-for-byte the frozen reviewed artifact, the record is approved against its exact checksum, and a clause-by-clause review is recorded. Delivery fidelity is 27/27 DELIVERS_REVIEWED_ARTIFACT with zero approved badges on non-reviewed content. Not blocking.

knownCaveats.title: 634 legacy plain_language_summary values are truncated mid-word
knownCaveats.detail: plain_language_summary is a hard 500-character cut of standard_text on 996 of 2,390 production rows, and 634 of those cut mid-word (1910.219 ends "...thirteen thirty-seconds () inch or less. 1/2 (2"). That fragment is what a Path B customer reads TODAY under the "HazLenz standard summary" label. Pre-existing and unrelated to governance. Not a SHADOW blocker (SHADOW is customer-invisible). Not a cutover blocker: cutover REPAIRS it for the 15 approved reviewed renderings and leaves it unchanged for unapproved records, which is the fallback contract promise.

knownCaveats: THE RUN-2 RECORDING PERSISTS 63 STRUCTURED FIELDS PER ROW AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS EVIDENCE. Any future phase planning a Tier-2 replay must check FIRST whether the change it wants to test depends on evidence text, a rationale, an uncertainty list or a clarification body -- because none of those exist in the recording, and three of the four G4 false-ACTIVE rows are indistinguishable in every recorded field from a correct ACTIVE row.

THE GATE TABLE IS NOT A SAFETY METRIC. G1 counts a high-consequence miss as "no validated candidate at all", so a change that keeps the candidate and strips its ACTIVE assertion is invisible to it. This phase measured exactly that: a scenario improving G4 and G9 while reducing high-consequence ACTIVE assertions. Remediation vetoes must be measured on the substance, never through the gates alone.

governedReleaseConstruction.architecture: Option C -- version-controlled governed source records PLUS an explicit release membership definition, staged through a session-scoped TEMP table inside the construction transaction.
governedReleaseConstruction.pipeline: governed-source-set.ts (zero DB access) -> release-definition.ts + definitions/*.json (explicit membership) -> TEMP staging (ON COMMIT DROP) -> regulatory_release_records (immutable) -> release-manifest.ts (UNCHANGED) -> reviewer decisions (UNCHANGED) -> eight activation gates (UNCHANGED) -> scripts/regulatory-release.ts (NEW operator CLI)
whyTempStagingNotAPersistedTable: no seventh migration, so the six KG-5A rehearsed migrations and old-code forward compatibility are untouched
cannot drift: staging is materialized from version-controlled sources microseconds before it is read
cannot leak: ON COMMIT DROP supplies most of the atomicity contract
orders and types exactly like standards_master, which is what makes manifest reproduction structural rather than a reimplementation of ICU collation and pg type mapping
governedReleaseConstruction.persistedInspectableArtifact: a PROVISIONAL release with its records written -- a real lifecycle state, reviewable through review:release-record, impossible to mistake for a finalized release
governedReleaseConstruction.legacyCorpusNonMutationInvariant: GOVERNED RELEASE CONSTRUCTION DOES NOT WRITE TO standards_master. Enforced by assertNoLegacyCorpusWrites() over every statement the builder issues, not merely documented.
governedReleaseConstruction.membershipMechanism: A version-controlled release definition names the exact member citationKeys. Membership is a lookup, never a scan. Adding, deleting or reordering any legacy corpus row cannot change the manifest -- measured.

operatorReleaseCommand.concurrencyModel: compare-and-swap: PointerMoveOptions.expectedCurrentReleaseId is re-checked INSIDE the transaction under pg_advisory_xact_lock. Additive -- the key absent preserves pre-KG-5B behaviour exactly.
operatorReleaseCommand.concurrencyDefectFoundAndFixed: The CLI first checked --expected-current outside the transaction. Two operators on the same stale reading both passed and both committed: every transaction atomic, one active release at the end, and still last-writer-wins. protectedConcurrencyInvariant.rule: --expected-current is compared inside the transaction, under pg_advisory_xact_lock, as a compare-and-swap. It may never be evaluated as a pre-flight read only.

rootCauseGovernance.statement: A failing test, comparator, harness, customer-path observation or production SHADOW discrepancy demonstrates a SYMPTOM. It does NOT by itself identify the component that must be modified.
requiredSequence: identify the authoritative layer that owns that contract
determine whether the implementation, source data, review state, resolver, presentation layer or instrumentation violates it
modify ONLY the owning layer unless evidence proves a cross-layer change is required
verify the correction at the boundary where the contract is observable
rootCauseGovernance.forbiddenLoop: observation -> edit -> rerun -> different observation -> edit again
prohibitions: Do not modify correct upstream or customer-facing behaviour to satisfy incorrect downstream instrumentation. If executable evidence proves the implementation satisfies the documented contract but a test or comparator disagrees, repair the test or comparator and classify the finding INSTRUMENTATION.
Do not reopen a protected architectural conclusion without new contradictory evidence.
Do not make multiple speculative edits across layers to make a metric turn green.
Do not weaken an invariant, threshold, predicate or production control to make a discrepancy disappear.
Do not create another KG implementation phase because a non-blocking defect was discovered.
rootCauseGovernance.instrumentationRepairProof: The proof that a repair was not made to move a number is that the verdict does not move. State the measured verdict before and after. An instrumentation repair that moves the verdict needs its own root-cause analysis.
rootCauseGovernance.ifRootCauseCannotBeEstablished: Classify UNCLASSIFIED, capture the evidence, and stop progression toward CUTOVER until resolved. Do not edit implementation to make an unexplained observation go away.
generalisedFrom: KG5A-DISC-01 (the missing WHERE clause was a symptom)
KG5C-FIX-01 (fix the field precedence, not severity)

architecturalOwnership.rule: Every newly discovered discrepancy must be assigned an architectural owner BEFORE implementation remediation. If ownership is unclear, investigate until it is established. Do not patch multiple layers because ownership has not yet been determined.
assignmentProcedure: state the observation as a contract violation, naming the contract
find the contract in the layer tables -> that is the owner
if it appears in two layers, the owner is the one closest to the contract's definition, not where the symptom surfaced
if it appears in none, the contract is undocumented: establish and document it before editing
record the owner in the open-issues register before remediation

findingClassification.rule: Exactly four top-level engineering dispositions. Every finding gets exactly one. Anything that does not fit is UNCLASSIFIED and stops progression toward CUTOVER until resolved.

BLOCKER.definition: A verified defect that prevents the next authorized release stage from being executed safely or truthfully.
BLOCKER.effect: Only a BLOCKER automatically expands the current release-gate work.
BLOCKER.note: Requires verification, not suspicion. Presumptive blockers: REVIEW_STATE_VIOLATION, CUSTOMER_MUTATION.

DEFECT_NONBLOCKING.definition: A real defect that does not invalidate the current release gate.
DEFECT_NONBLOCKING.effect: Record it, assign ownership, preserve it in openIssues for appropriate remediation.
prohibitions: Do NOT automatically create another KG phase for it.
Do NOT silently close it because a later stage happens to mask it.

INSTRUMENTATION.definition: The implementation satisfies the authoritative contract, but the measurement, comparator, test or harness does not measure that contract correctly.
INSTRUMENTATION.effect: Repair the instrumentation. Do not change correct production behaviour.
INSTRUMENTATION.note: State the measured verdict before and after. An instrumentation repair that moves the verdict needs its own root-cause analysis; it may be masking a real defect.

EXPECTED_EXPLAINED.definition: The observed difference is an expected consequence of the verified architecture.
EXPECTED_EXPLAINED.effect: No remediation required. Record enough explanation to prevent future rediscovery.
currentExamples: the Path A / Path B representation difference

discipline: 'Different' and 'wrong' are not the same claim.
A category may not be invented after seeing results to make an outcome look better.
A disposition may be revised only on new evidence, and the revision is recorded with it.

supersededFindings.purpose: Prevent a future session from rediscovering old evidence and reopening a resolved architectural question. This is NOT a suppression mechanism: new contradictory evidence always wins over documentation. Each entry names the exact condition that would justify reopening it.

KG5B-DISC-01.originalObservation: Legacy and governed representations differ for governed citations; 15 of 27 approved records measured CONTENT_DIFFERENCE / BLOCKING.

The count of 15 is confirmed by re-measurement through the real customer path on both body-text tiers. All 15 classify GOVERNED_REVIEWED_RENDERING. The customer receives exactly the reviewed governed artifact.
KG5B-DISC-01.whyByteEqualityIsUnreachable: Legacy standard_text is a verbatim eCFR/MSHA ingest; the governed canonicalText is the reviewed rendering KG-3D/3E/4A adjudicated clause by clause. Byte-equality is not achievable by construction, so its absence is not evidence of disagreement.
KG5B-DISC-01.whatItDoesNotAssert: This classification does NOT assert that the human review was substantively correct. It reports that the delivered artifact is the reviewed one and that a review exists; never that the review was right.
KG5B-DISC-01.scopeLimit: The eight unreviewed records cannot receive this classification. Entry requires a recorded clause review, so the 3 unreviewed records whose legacy row resolves are refused the category and classify CONTENT_DIFFERENCE.
KG5B-DISC-01.protectedConclusion: Do NOT attempt to make governed content byte-identical to legacy content merely to eliminate this difference. Doing so would replace a reviewed artifact with an unreviewed ingest under a 'Verified standard text' badge, inverting the purpose of the governance subsystem.

KG5A-DISC-01.protectedConclusion: Do not 'fix' release construction by adding filters to a query over standards_master. Governed membership is explicit in release-definition.ts, never inferred from database contents.

a manifest fails to reproduce from the version-controlled definition

productionShadowProtocol.note: Everything here is frozen BEFORE production SHADOW is enabled, deliberately. Defining what counts as success after seeing results is how an observation becomes a rationalization. This section does NOT authorize production SHADOW.
productionShadowProtocol.primaryHypothesis: H0 - On real production requests and real production data, the governed resolver operating observationally selects and constructs governed results consistent with the verified release and customer-delivery contracts, while LEGACY remains the sole authoritative customer response.

H1_citationResolution.hypothesis: For every request, resolvedCitation === requestedCitation; citation identity is never silently broadened or collapsed; subsection requests never fall back to a base citation.
H1_citationResolution.refutedBy: any CITATION_DIFFERENCE, or a base-citation fallback for a subsection request

H2_approvedArtifactDelivery.hypothesis: For every approved record, the governed artifact the resolver constructs is byte-identical to the frozen payload.canonicalText of the pinned release record.
H2_approvedArtifactDelivery.refutedBy: a governed construction that differs from the frozen artifact

H3_unreviewedFallback.hypothesis: For every unreviewed record, governed delivery is withheld and legacy behaviour is preserved exactly.
H3_unreviewedFallback.refutedBy: any governed content constructed for a record with no effective approval

H4_resolverPathBehaviour.hypothesis: Both paths resolve through the single seam and therefore cannot disagree - this is STRUCTURAL (they share resolveStandard()), and SHADOW telemetry does NOT independently re-establish it: the v2 event carries no resolver-path identifier (KG5D-DISC-01). What SHADOW can evaluate is that every observation's resolution is internally consistent with its own pinned release, and that the Path A / Path B representation difference accounts for every content-length difference observed.
H4_resolverPathBehaviour.refutedBy: an observation whose backing, citation or release is inconsistent with its own pinned release

H5_badgeAndProvenanceTruthfulness.hypothesis: customerVisible is false throughout, projectGovernedDisplay() contributes {}, and no governed provenance is written; knowledgeReleaseId is NULL on every row.
H5_badgeAndProvenanceTruthfulness.refutedBy: any governed key in a payload, or any non-NULL provenance

H6_absenceOfCustomerMutation.hypothesis: The customer receives the pristine legacy run on every request; the stable field set is identical to LEGACY; customerOutputUnchanged is true on every event.
H6_absenceOfCustomerMutation.refutedBy: any difference in a field derived as stable, or an INDETERMINATE invariance check

H7_instrumentationFidelity.hypothesis: Telemetry distinguishes legacy from governed representations, attributes every observation to its correlation, finding and pinned release, and every event passes the v2 privacy guard. Resolver-path attribution is OUT OF SCOPE - the field does not exist.
H7_instrumentationFidelity.refutedBy: a comparison that cannot name its release, or a field outside the v2 allowlist

H8_releaseIdentity.hypothesis: Every observation names the single explicitly intended release and its manifest checksum, captured in the same query as the active-pointer read.
H8_releaseIdentity.refutedBy: any observation naming a different release, or a manifest/pointer mismatch

productionShadowProtocol.hypothesisEvaluationRule: A hypothesis is evaluated, not assumed. A hypothesis with zero qualifying observations is UNPROVEN, never 'passed'. The KG-4D per-observation non-vacuity floor (D-54) applies: three slices have been fooled by an equality oracle comparing two broken observations.
productionShadowProtocol.everyObservationMustMapToAHypothesis: Every SHADOW observation must map to a predefined hypothesis or be explicitly classified as an unexpected observation. Vague goals such as 'see what happens in production' are not permitted.

EXPECTED_EQUIVALENCE.definition: Governed and legacy outcomes are materially equivalent under the applicable contract.

EXPECTED_GOVERNED_REVIEWED_RENDERING.definition: The governed representation differs from legacy but exactly matches the reviewed governed artifact. This is NOT a defect merely because the bytes differ.
entryRequirements: reviewer-approved in the active release against the exact checksum
a clause-by-clause review recorded in a named KG phase artifact
the delivered text byte-identical to the frozen payload.canonicalText

RESOLUTION_DIFFERENCE.definition: Legacy and governed paths select materially different citation identities or applicability outcomes.

CONTENT_DIFFERENCE.definition: For a record expected to satisfy the same content contract, the delivered governed artifact differs unexpectedly.

MISSING_GOVERNED_RECORD.definition: A request expected to resolve through an approved governed record cannot do so.
MISSING_GOVERNED_RECORD.defaultDisposition: investigate; may be DEFECT_NONBLOCKING corpus backlog

REVIEW_STATE_VIOLATION.definition: Unreviewed content is treated as approved/governed customer content, or approval state is otherwise misrepresented.

CUSTOMER_MUTATION.definition: SHADOW changes the authoritative customer response or customer-visible behaviour.

INSTRUMENTATION_ERROR.definition: The comparator, telemetry or harness is observing the wrong field, representation, citation identity or lifecycle state - measuring the wrong contract.
INSTRUMENTATION_ERROR.defaultDisposition: INSTRUMENTATION; repair the measurement, not production

UNCLASSIFIED.definition: The evidence does not fit an existing category. Do not immediately edit implementation; capture the evidence and perform root-cause classification first.

productionShadowProtocol.taxonomyIsFrozen: Do NOT invent new categories after observing results merely to make SHADOW appear successful. If a genuinely new category is required, document why the frozen taxonomy was insufficient - the taxonomy being wrong is itself a result.
productionShadowProtocol.taxonomyRelationshipToEngineTaxonomy: This is the OPERATIONAL layer above the 15-category engine taxonomy in shadow-comparison.ts. They are not competing vocabularies: the engine taxonomy classifies a comparison; this taxonomy classifies a finding an operator must act on.

abortGates.rule: SHADOW must be aborted if evidence indicates any of the following.
conditions: customer responses are being modified (any CUSTOMER_MUTATION)
SHADOW can influence the authoritative resolver result
an unreviewed governed artifact can be presented as approved
release identity is not the explicitly intended release
citation identity is being silently broadened or collapsed
production writes occur where observation is required to be read-only
the comparator cannot reliably distinguish legacy from governed representations

telemetry cannot attribute an observation to its correlation, finding and pinned release (deliberately NOT 'cannot identify the resolver path': the v2 event carries no resolver-path identifier at all per KG5D-DISC-01, so that stronger wording would abort every run on its first event; path-level attribution is a known instrumentation limit, not an abort condition)
release/rollback state differs from the expected preflight state
an unexpected condition makes continued observation unsafe or uninterpretable
abortGates.doNotContinueForALargerSample: Do NOT continue collecting data after a hard abort condition merely to obtain a larger sample. A larger sample of uninterpretable observations is not more evidence.

mechanics.killSwitch: engages on ANY non-empty value including off/false/0 (D-40: brakes are permissive, only locks are exact)
mechanics.circuitBreaker: hard invariants trip at threshold zero with no sample floor (D-42)
mechanics.indeterminateCheck: a missing or indeterminate invariance check is itself a hard violation (D-43): unverified is not verified

successCriteria.rule: A controlled production SHADOW stage is successful ONLY if all of the following hold.
criteria: every observed difference is classified into the frozen taxonomy; none left unclassified
every EXPECTED_GOVERNED_REVIEWED_RENDERING result verified against the actual reviewed governed artifact (the frozen payload.canonicalText, not a re-derivation)
instrumentation proven to measure the customer contract correctly, including a per-observation non-vacuity floor
LEGACY remained the authoritative customer response for the entire observation window
SHADOW was disabled cleanly after the observation window
the evidence is sufficient to make a separate CUTOVER decision
successCriteria.successIsNotZeroByteDifferences: SHADOW success is NOT 'zero byte differences'. That criterion would contradict the verified KG-5C architecture, under which the governed artifact SHOULD differ from the unreviewed legacy ingest for every reviewed rendering. Adopting it would create direct pressure to replace reviewed content with unreviewed content to make a number go to zero.
successCriteria.completionIsNotCutoverAuthorization: SHADOW completion is NOT automatic CUTOVER authorization. CUTOVER is a separate explicit human decision taken after this evidence exists, and it additionally requires openIssues.KG4E-DISC-03 to be closed.

doNot: weaken an invariant to make a discrepancy disappear

rootCauses.R1_impressionGatePolarity: checkSubjectiveImpression refused ACTIVE unless a word from the 30-entry FACTUAL_CONDITION_TOKENS appeared unhedged. 'sheared' is absent, so H-AM-05 was deleted. Proven with two isolating fixtures, one containing zero negations so the R2 change provably cannot reach it.
rootCauses.R1_newEvidence_secondDeathPath: H-AM-05 also dies through SEMANTIC_NEGATION_UNADDRESSED when the model picks a NARROW factual span, because 'not' scopes across the bare 'and'. L3-2b's NEXT_ACTION.md attributed it to the impression gate alone. This is the SECOND time a phase has found the prior phase's single attribution incomplete (see l32bBinderPrecision B08).
rootCauses.R1_newEvidence_entryConditionAlsoAList: The gate only ran when a phrase from SUBJECTIVE_IMPRESSION_TOKENS appeared. 'struck me as' is absent, so H-AM-01 was ADMITTED as ACTIVE with no gate run at all — a latent false ACTIVE that L3-2b's pipeline result concealed because its model returned no candidate. Recorded as L3-2C-DISC-01.
rootCauses.R2_bareConjunctionScope: negationScopes() applied hasPredicate() at commas and nowhere else; 'and' appeared in CLAUSE_STARTERS only as 'and separately'. Measured: 'no' governs 'no LOTO is applied and the guard is missing' in full. The proving fixture contains no subjective language, so the R1 change cannot reach it.
rootCauses.R3_clarification: Two different failures behind 'recall 1 of 3': H-AM-01 produced NO candidate at all so nothing could carry a question, and H-AM-02 produced ACTIVE with clarification null. On H-AM-02 the binder raised SEMANTIC_CLARIFICATION_EXPECTED_NOT_SUPPLIED and then deleted the candidate, destroying the only carrier the question could travel on.

repairs.R1: Gate POLARITY inverted. New impression-scope.ts classifies predication segments structurally as IMPRESSION / OBSERVER_ACTION / FACTUAL / NEITHER and refuses ACTIVE only when an impression is present and NO segment states a plain fact. NO condition vocabulary is consulted at any point.
repairs.R2: hasPredicate() applied at bare conjunctions, held to a STRICTER test than the comma: only a finite verb ends scope there, because a bare 'and' is the ordinary way to continue a negated list. 'or' and 'nor' never end scope.
repairs.R3a: The impression branch moved INTO the condition-state ladder as a required output shape, which is what lifted recall to 3/3.
repairs.R3b: DEMOTION replaces deletion for SEMANTIC_SUBJECTIVE_IMPRESSION_NOT_ACTIVE alone and only from ACTIVE: the candidate is kept at INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE carrying a clarification derived from its own cited evidence. Any other fatal code still deletes. This is NOT a redesign of clarification transport — a clarification remains a field on a hazard candidate.

l32cGatePolarity.whyPositiveVocabularyAdmissionWasReplace: English has an unbounded supply of ways to say a thing is broken, so every word missing from an admission list deletes a real hazard; the L3-2b holdout proved that costs a high-consequence finding. The remaining vocabularies sit on the IMPRESSION side, where a missing word costs precision — measurable against negative controls and recoverable — rather than a hazard. That asymmetry is the mechanism, not an implementation detail.
loadBearingImplementationRules: OBSERVER_ACTION must be distinct from IMPRESSION, or 'I saw the guard was missing' is deleted.
The hedge test must run BEFORE the predication test: 'may be cut' carries no recognised finite verb, and a predication-first order let H-AM-02 through as ACTIVE.
A copula does not count as a predication preceding a hedge: 'the drum IS possibly leaking' is hedged.

The clarification axis is now PERFECT on fresh sealed evidence (TP 3, FP 0, FN 0 -- precision and recall both 100%), all seven proven E1 defects are closed with all six paired counter-fixtures still refusing, the L3-2c holdout recovers 47->53 of 54, and sealed family coverage went from 15 to 23 of 24 taxonomy families. rootCauses.E1_theTwoChecksAreNotTheSameDefect: PROVEN, 12 fixtures, 7 defects. checkContradiction uses vocabulary to REJECT -- a false positive DELETES a hazard (5 reproduced, 3 high-consequence). checkStateSupported uses it to ADMIT a state the model already claimed -- a false positive ACCEPTS A WRONG STATE (2 reproduced, NEITHER PREVIOUSLY DOCUMENTED).
rootCauses.E1_newEvidence_admissionDirection: Section 34.6 documented the syntactic-role defect only as a DELETION mechanism. It runs in the ADMISSION direction too: CORRECTED accepted on a modifier, and CONTROLLED accepted on 'no guardrail was in place' -- a live hazard labelled controlled, which at the customer tier is a missed hazard wearing a reassuring label.
rootCauses.E1_substringMatch: HAZARD_NEGATION_OBJECTS was matched with `governed.includes(o)` -- a SUBSTRING test, not word-boundary. That detail causes L3-2E-DISC-06 below.
rootCauses.E2_clausePosition: PROVEN BY ABLATION, and it CONTRADICTS section 34.5. D-NG-04 with the negation REMOVED still fails; with the clause MOVED it passes. The mechanism is CLAUSE POSITION -- the observation is classified from its FIRST clause -- not an oscillation between rungs. D-NG-04 and D-CR-04 are one defect seen from two sides.
rootCauses.E2_cellB_alreadyCorrect: A 4-cell discriminator matrix varying unobserved-fact-present against is-it-deciding INDEPENDENTLY found cell B (unobserved but NOT deciding) already correct 3 of 3 BEFORE any repair. Direct evidence against any global change in clarification pressure.
rootCauses.E2_fixtureLabelCorrection: E2-D-01 was first labelled clarificationExpected true for 'Looked at the chemical store on the way past.' That contradicts the H-AM-04 precedent ('Walked the yard.', FALSE): with nothing to suspect there is nothing to ask about. The label was wrong, not the engine. Corrected in development BEFORE sealing and recorded.

repairs.E1_predicateRole: New predicate-role.ts classifies a matched token as ASSERTED_PREDICATE, NEGATED_PREDICATE, ATTRIBUTIVE_MODIFIER, NP_HEAD or OTHER, by position and morphology. Bounded, hand-rolled, no parser and no dependency -- the same class of analyser as negation-scope.ts and impression-scope.ts.
repairs.E1_contradictionScope: checkContradiction now requires an ASSERTED, UNNEGATED predicate, and draws removal tokens from a strict UNAMBIGUOUS_SERVICE_WITHDRAWAL subset. Bare 'removed' is EXCLUDED because 'the chain guard has been removed' and 'the conveyor was removed from service' are both asserted predicates and only the second withdraws equipment. The negated-hazard test additionally requires the negated phrase's HEAD to be the hazard object (English NPs are head-final, so 'hazard warning labels' denies *labels*, a control) and NO contrastive connector after the scope.
repairs.E1_stateSupportScope: checkStateSupported requires an ASSERTED, unnegated predicate for CORRECTED, CONTROLLED and REMOVED_FROM_SERVICE. NEGATED and HYPOTHETICAL deliberately keep presence semantics -- their markers are particles, not verbs predicated of a subject.
repairs.E1_governingAsymmetry: A vocabulary used to REJECT must be unambiguous; a vocabulary used to ADMIT may be permissive. Section 33.1's lesson one level down, and it is what justifies the different treatment of the two checks.
repairs.E2_prompt: The ladder rule generalised from 'a negation governs only its own clause' to 'EVALUATE EVERY CLAUSE, NOT ONLY THE FIRST -- let the strongest condition claim decide', plus a five-line discriminator: is the thing that could not be observed the fact that DECIDES this candidate? decides it -> INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE with a question; decides nothing -> classify from what WAS observed and ask nothing.
repairs.E2_detectorRecordsOnly: observation-availability.ts detects EXPLICITLY_NOT_OBSERVED / OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE / UNSPECIFIED and records them as an ADVISORY issue. It changes NO condition state and removes NO candidate, exactly as the entry contract required. An inability phrase counts only when attached to a PERCEPTION verb, so 'the guard could not be refitted' is not an observation gap; 'failed to' was excluded because equipment fails as readily as inspectors do.

checkScopes.checkContradiction: (A) ACTIVE resting on a negated hazard: fires only when the negated NP HEAD is a hazard object AND no contrastive connector follows the scope. (B) ACTIVE contradicted by a correction or service withdrawal: fires only on an ASSERTED, UNNEGATED predicate drawn from CORRECTION_TOKENS or UNAMBIGUOUS_SERVICE_WITHDRAWAL.
checkScopes.checkStateSupported: CORRECTED / CONTROLLED / REMOVED_FROM_SERVICE require an asserted unnegated predicate; NEGATED / HYPOTHETICAL keep presence semantics.
checkScopes.modifierNegatedNonPredicateHandling: A modifier, a label/name, an object of a preposition and a token under a governing negation may NOT delete or create a finding. Only an asserted predicate may act on the rejection path.

l32eSyntacticRole.observationAvailabilityModel: Four values -- OBSERVED (implicit), EXPLICITLY_NOT_OBSERVED, OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE, UNSPECIFIED -- kept SEPARATE from CONDITION_EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT. Availability informs uncertainty and is recorded; it never determines condition state. A clarification is owed only when the unobserved fact is DECISION-CRITICAL for the candidate.

rootCauses.F1_predicateHoodIsNotListMembership: PROVEN pre-patch. hasPredicate() recognised a predicate through 24 auxiliaries plus a participle regex. One sentence, one lexical verb apart, scoped two ways: "the fitter WENT inside" ran the negation to offset 147, "the fitter WAS inside" ended it at the comma at 50. The binder then deleted a high-consequence confined-space finding with SEMANTIC_NEGATION_UNADDRESSED. Lexical verbs are an OPEN class and cannot be enumerated; FINITENESS is decidable from regular morphology plus the CLOSED inventory of irregular past forms.
rootCauses.F2_isTheSameMechanismAsF1: PROVEN. NP_TERMINATORS omitted `against`, `beyond` and `per` — three measured failures, not one word. Function words are a GENUINELY CLOSED class, so completing them is complete rather than incomplete. F1, F2 and F3 are ONE mechanism in three functions and are repaired once, in word-classes.ts.
rootCauses.F3_wasTwoFaultsComposing: PROVEN. nounPhraseHead returned the trailing participle `issued`, and head.includes(o) then matched `issue` inside it. Either alone was survivable. Substring containment is an UNBOUNDED admission rule; the same shape was measured on harm/harmless, concern/concerning, access/accessory.

representationBoundClarificationFinding.invariant: A CLARIFICATION CAN ONLY BE CARRIED ON A hazardCandidate
representationBoundClarificationFinding.mechanism: When the model correctly concludes the observation is underdetermined and returns INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE with an EMPTY hazardCandidates array, the contract gives the clarification nowhere to live. The reasoning did not change; only whether there was a carrier for it.
representationBoundClarificationFinding.scope: This is the WHOLE of Gemini's measured instability. Both order-sensitivity scenarios and the single noise-floor scenario are this one mechanism.
representationBoundClarificationFinding.classification: CONTRACT_REPRESENTATION_BOUND, with a structural cause a provider swap cannot fix. It is NOT the mechanism section 37.5 proposed, and it is preserved as its own label rather than folded into the terminal letter.

orderSensitivityQualification.qualification1: The margin is 2 against a floor of 1. ONE scenario separates signal from noise, and a margin that small cannot carry a strong claim.

orderSensitivityQualification.rule: Gemini improves the pre-registered incoherence axis materially and decisively, and improves the order-sensitivity axis narrowly and conditionally. Terminal A stands under the pre-registered rule. It does not stand more strongly than that.

l32jCarrierActivation.rootCauseOfTheRegression: Declaration revision 1 told the model the field was for when you 'return an EMPTY hazardCandidates array', and the model read that as permission to return one. Two rules pointed opposite ways and the newer, more specific one won, pulling scenarios off the ACTIVE rung onto the empty-INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE path. Dropping the candidate ALSO defeated section 34.2's MUST-NOT-ASK gate, which only fires when candidates exist and all are decided.

fwc09.geminiTrace: candidate machine_guarding_bypassed_two_hand_control, conditionState ACTIVE, rationale 'Strapping it down bypasses the control, making the hazard active. fwc09.theDeterministicLayerAlreadyHeldTheFact: control-adequacy.ts recorded CONTROL_ABSENT with matchedTerm 'strapped down' on that very candidate in that very run. Section 36.4 fixed that module as RECORDING ONLY (L3-INV-12, the section 35.2 restraint). The provider inverted the phrase, the deterministic layer read it correctly, filed an advisory, and the hazard was deleted anyway. DO NOT read this as an instruction to make it decide.
fwc09.theControlDiscriminates: F-WC-03 ran in the SAME PROCESS on the same prompt and schema, produced the same CONTROL_ABSENT advisory ('missing'), and because the model chose ACTIVE was kept and delivered. Identical pipeline, opposite outcome, decided entirely by the state choice. Without this control the finding would be D-54-vacuous.
fwc09.proposedOrRejected: MODEL PROPOSED, DETERMINISTIC PIPELINE REJECTED. NOT a candidate omission and NOT a validator rejection. The two must never be called 'a model miss' interchangeably.
fwc09.amplifier: SEMANTIC_BINDER -- a CORRECT refusal of an unsupported state DELETES the candidate rather than demoting it. Recorded separately; the binder is exonerated as the origin by the F-WC-03 control.
fwc09.deterministic: YES -- CONTROLLED is the sole state in 13 of the 14 recorded qwen ladder-family runs across six artifacts and four sessions, plus 2 of 2 this phase. The one exception is V_A_LADDER built on the REJECTED v7 declaration (a76debe5), which returned ['CONTROLLED','ACTIVE'] -- recorded because a rejected prompt's behaviour is evidence, not a recommendation, and D-59 is NOT reopened by it.
fwc09.orderSensitive: NO -- V_A_LADDER on the v6 base also returns CONTROLLED
fwc09.occursBeforeOrAfterValidation: the fault is BEFORE validation; the loss is AFTER it

ccs05.observation: If the level probe on the caustic tank were to fail closed during a transfer, the vent could pressurise and lift the manway gasket. Pole: CLARIFICATION_MUST_NOT_ASK.
ccs05.design: EIGHT isolated processes, FOUR per variant. Variant A is section 36.7's already-open one-block move, reconstructed by the locked harness's own manipulation and PINNED to the sha256 the frozen L3-2g artifact recorded (a6dea73f); the instrument refuses to run otherwise.
ccs05.variantB_shipped: conditionState HYPOTHETICAL 4 of 4; NO question raised 4 of 4; final carries no question 4 of 4
ccs05.variantA_section36_7: question raised 4 of 4; conditionState demoted to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE 1 of 4 and HYPOTHETICAL 3 of 4; section 34.2's gate fired 3 of 4; final carries a false question 1 of 4
ccs05.twoEffectsNotOne: THE BLOCK MOVE makes qwen raise a MUST-NOT-ASK question DETERMINISTICALLY (4/4) -- that is the real section 36.7 signal and it is not noise. SEPARATELY, on BYTE-IDENTICAL variant-A prompts in separate processes, qwen returns a different conditionState 1 time in 4 -- provider variance at temperature 0 with a pinned seed, NOT an effect of block order. THE CUSTOMER-VISIBLE FAILURE NEEDS BOTH. The single-shot L3-2g comparison had no variant-A repeat control and could not see this.
ccs05.whyTheGateCannotCatchIt: clarificationBelongsHere returns true iff the state is in L3_UNDECIDED_STATES. Section 34.2 made that exemption DELIBERATELY so a candidate demoted to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE keeps the question it was demoted to carry. Section 41.3 recorded the DROP form of the defeat (rev 1 removed the candidate, so the gate never fired); this phase measures the DEMOTE form (the candidate survives at an undecided state and the gate is inert for the same structural reason). Two mechanically unrelated perturbations, one structural route.
ccs05.theGateIsLoadBearingNotLax: On the same 24-scenario cohort the undecided-state exemption is exactly what lets all 5 of 5 CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED scenarios (F-OA-01, F-OA-02, F-CL-01, F-CL-03, B10) carry their legitimate question, on both providers. The exemption is doing its job five times for every one time it is exploited.
ccs05.vacuityControlIsMeasured: In the THREE variant-A runs where the state came back HYPOTHETICAL the gate DID fire -- SEMANTIC_CLARIFICATION_ON_DECIDED_STATE, clarificationsDropped populated, question suppressed. The gate demonstrably works and is demonstrably unreachable when the state is undecided. This is measured, not argued.
ccs05.fieldLevelVsSemanticDecision: BOTH ARE PRESENT AT DIFFERENT TIERS AND MUST NEVER BE REPORTED AS ONE NUMBER. At the MODEL tier the difference is a DETERMINISTIC FIELD-LEVEL difference (4/4, raisedClarification). At the SHIPPED DECISION tier it is SEMANTIC DECISION VARIANCE (1/4) -- a false question reaches a safety professional. The hazard decision, false ACTIVE and high-consequence axes NEVER move: assertsActive is false in all eight runs.
ccs05.theQuestionIsRealNotVacuous: 'Is the level probe on the caustic tank currently failing closed during a transfer?' -- a plausible, answerable question that the scenario's own conditional phrasing already answers, which is exactly why the pole is MUST-NOT-ASK.
ccs05.changedBlockIsSemantic: YES -- it is the ABSENT-CONTROLS + CONTROL-ADEQUACY material, not formatting or ordering. Section 36.7 measured the same trade from the other end.
ccs05.primaryBoundary: ASSERTION_STATE_SELECTION -- provider stage, the SAME boundary as F-WC-09
ccs05.composition: SEMANTIC_BINDER -- section 34.2's undecided-state exemption defeated by the demotion
ccs05.generalizationRisk: C-CS-05 is the ONLY scenario in the 24-scenario cohort producing a HYPOTHETICAL candidate, on EITHER provider, so it is the only place on this cohort where the composition has anything to act on.
ccs05.section24Disposition: DEFECT_NONBLOCKING -- the shipped configuration is variant B, under which the failure does not occur in 4 of 4 runs.

l32kShippedResidualRootCause.whatTheTwoCasesShare: BOTH SHIPPED-PATH RESIDUALS ARE THE MODEL'S SINGLE-ENUM conditionState CHOICE, NOT ITS FACTS. Neither is a candidate omission, an evidence-binding failure, a validator rejection, a resolver fault or a scorer artifact. In both the model proposes the right hazard on cleanly bound evidence and then selects the wrong state, and in both something in the system already held the fact that decides it: control-adequacy.ts's CONTROL_ABSENT and V_S_STRUCT's controlReading DEFEATED for F-WC-09; its own other three runs' HYPOTHETICAL for C-CS-05. Section 42.6 recorded that TERMINAL_A's decisive axis is not measurable on the shipped ladder; this is the shipped-path evidence that the ladder's single-enum state selection is where qwen loses both cases while the separated-fact representation answers both correctly. IT IS TWO SCENARIOS AND IT IS NOT A MANDATE -- section 36.7's measured trade stands, section 37.11 item 2 stands, and nothing here promotes a representation, a resolver ordering or a provider.

structuralFinding.rule: checkStateSupported CAN ONLY EVER REFUSE A NON-ACTIVE STATE, so delete-versus-demote cannot move any hard section 29.8 gate.
structuralFinding.consequence: The check cannot prevent a false ACTIVE. Every candidate it deletes was already non-asserting, and demotion moves it to another non-asserting state. Hazard detection, false ACTIVE and the high-consequence axis are all computed from asserts = some candidate at ACTIVE, so the disposition is a NULL MOVE on all three -- including on F-WC-09, the case that motivated the question.

inventory.fwc09Placement: F-WC-09 is ONE OF FOUR distinct high-consequence identities this code has deleted, not the only case. Section 43.2's account of it reproduces exactly at the shipped path.
inventory.negativeControlCharacter: On the 39 negative-control rows the MODEL'S STATE CHOICE IS RIGHT and the binder's refusal is wrong on its own terms -- D02 ('locked out with each worker's personal lock'), B14, H-OF7, DEV-28. Deletion still yields the expected customer outcome because a controlled hazard and a deleted hazard are BOTH non-asserting. This is a D-54 agreement: the right outcome reached by a reason unrelated to the scenario's semantics.

authorityAnalysis.generalRule: A REFUSAL MAY DEMOTE TO AN UNDECIDED STATE ONLY WHERE THE REFUSAL ITSELF ESTABLISHED THAT THE DECISION IS OPEN.
authorityAnalysis.whyTheImpressionGateQualifies: checkSubjectiveImpression establishes positively that no predication in the cited evidence asserts a condition of the thing observed -- nothing was asserted -- and raises SEMANTIC_CLARIFICATION_EXPECTED_NOT_SUPPLIED in the same breath. Demotion asserts nothing the check did not prove (section 33.4).
authorityAnalysis.whyCheckStateSupportedDoesNot: It establishes only that the marker vocabulary for the claimed state is absent, asserted, from the cited span. It makes no finding about whether anything was asserted and raises no clarification expectation. Demoting would assert 'the decision was not made' -- FALSE on 39 of 52 measured rows. That is deterministic SEMANTIC INFERENCE, not deterministic VALIDATION, and a conclusion the provider never proposed (L3-INV-08).
authorityAnalysis.A_DELETE: PERMITTED -- pure refusal, asserts nothing, invents nothing.
authorityAnalysis.B_DEMOTE_TO_UNDECIDED: NOT PERMITTED under this check -- L3-INV-08.
authorityAnalysis.C_REDERIVE_DECIDED_STATE: FORBIDDEN TWICE -- invents a decided conclusion the provider never proposed (L3-INV-08) and manufactures ACTIVE from a state the binder merely failed to read (L3-INV-04).
authorityAnalysis.D_PRESERVE_CANDIDATE_REJECT_STATE: COLLAPSES INTO B -- L3_UNDECIDED_STATES is the contract's only representation of 'unresolved', and section 34.2 fixes the other six states as the decision. There is no third thing to move the candidate to without inventing one.
authorityAnalysis.controlAdequacyRefused: controlAdequacy separates the poles where it speaks (6 real-hazard rows against 1 negative control) and is REFUSED on three independent grounds: it is silent on 33 of 52 rows so cannot carry a general rule; using it to decide would give a deliberately advisory module decision authority, which L3-INV-12, section 35.2, section 36.4 and section 43.4 each fix in place; and it would recover ZERO high-consequence misses anyway. control-adequacy.ts REMAINS RECORDING-ONLY.

measuredCounterfactual.basis: All 52 distinct (scenario, proposed-state) pairs, using the SHIPPED scorer semantics read from score-l32f-reasoning.ts.
measuredCounterfactual.conclusion: B and D are STRICTLY DOMINATED by A: they move the high-consequence axis by ZERO and pay 39 preserved negative-control candidates and up to 31 unnecessary clarifications for it, against an axis held at 100% precision since L3-2d and identified by section 36.7 as the binding trade. C closes the high-consequence axis and introduces 39 FALSE ACTIVE on the same rows.

l32lSemanticStateDisposition.deletionCostNotMinimised: Deletion is RETAINED, not exonerated. On the four high-consequence identities the customer receives NO hazard record at all rather than a candidate with its evidence and an open question (section 43.2) -- a real loss no shipped-scorer axis captures, because both outcomes are non-asserting. It is NOT repairable at the binder: it originates at D-63's provider-stage single-enum conditionState choice, and the binder cannot correct a wrong decided state without making a decided claim of its own.

architecturalPurposeOfClarification.mechanism: Section 34.2: the eight condition states divide exactly -- INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and UNKNOWN say the decision was not made, the other six ARE the decision. architecturalPurposeOfClarification.classification: A safety-quality and user-efficiency defect, deterministically contained. NOT a safety-authority failure: the remedy for a misplaced question is to drop the question and keep the hazard, which is not how a safety-authority failure is handled.
architecturalPurposeOfClarification.section298: Section 29.8's hard-zero acceptance list contains NO clarification rate of either kind.

recallVsPrecision.recall: Question was required -- did HazLenz raise it? Failure means uncertainty travels unflagged. NO downstream deterministic catch: a question not asked cannot be recovered. Stays HARD-GATED at 100%.
recallVsPrecision.precision: HazLenz raised a question -- was it necessary? A breach of the decision boundary is refused by the validator BEFORE anyone sees it; a question inside the boundary is one the contract permits. Deterministically contained either way.
recallVsPrecision.decidingAxis: They differ on whether the failure is deterministically containable. That is why they do not merit identical hard-gate treatment.

acceptanceRunPrivacyRule.basis: Section 37.10, a section explicitly titled 'IDENTIFIED, CHARACTERISED, NOT OPENED', plus the source of reasoning-input-builder.ts.
acceptanceRunPrivacyRule.materialFactSection455DidNotHave: Section 45.5 characterised hosted egress as 'inspector-authored narrative prose'. For the SEALED CORPUS that is not what it is: section 37.10 records safescope-gauntlet.source.v1.json as 150 rows DERIVED FROM REAL REGULATOR RECORDS -- 66 fatality reports, 51 inspection violations, 33 investigation summaries, OSHA 84 / MSHA 66.
acceptanceRunPrivacyRule.consequenceA: No InSite customer, site, account, user or inspection is represented. Section 10 and section 31.2 govern CUSTOMER data, and the sealed run transmits NONE. That is why the run is permissible at all.
acceptanceRunPrivacyRule.consequenceB: But it is real, not synthetic. Published regulator narratives name EMPLOYERS, FACILITIES and LOCATIONS, which the seven-rule pattern redactor does NOT catch. Section 45.5 said exactly this; it is now known to be load-bearing rather than hypothetical.
acceptanceRunPrivacyRule.builderIsStructuralAndUnbypassable: reasoning-input-builder.ts is 'the ONLY sanctioned way to construct a ReasoningInput'; exclusion is STRUCTURAL ('there is no argument through which a customer name, a site address, an account id ... can enter, because no such parameter exists'); and ALL THREE locked harnesses import it (activate-l32j-shipped-corpus.ts, diagnose-l32k-shipped-residual.ts, ablate-l32g-state-separation.ts).
acceptanceRunPrivacyRule.redactionRunsBeforeCanonicalisation: So evidence offsets index the redacted string and a returned span can never quote text that was never sent.
THE_RULE: 1. The sanctioned builder (2865ae91a7f50ff5794ea5d116399662e01116a2e9f34a585ac0ff276dbccc9e) is MANDATORY. No path may bypass it, and no harness may be modified to avoid it.
2. hazlenz.l3.redaction.v1 runs on every row, and redactionVersion plus per-rule counts are recorded in the acceptance evidence for EVERY row, including rows where the count is zero.
3. NO customer data is transmitted, by construction. Section 10 / section 31.2's customer-data boundary is NOT ENGAGED by the sealed run.

G3_denominators.truthAssignmentTable: clarificationExpected is assigned ONCE at build time, never inferred from text: INDEPENDENT_GAUNTLET -> false (the source declares no ambiguity field and none may be inferred); INDEPENDENT_REALISM -> row.shouldHaveMissingEvidence === true (strict identity; false -> false; ABSENT -> false); AUTHORED_CONTROL -> the value frozen for its family.
G3_denominators.absentIsNotUnknown: Absent is not unknown and absent is not true. The 28 realism rows without the field are clarificationExpected: false. Treating absence as ambiguity would silently enlarge a hard-gated denominator with rows whose truth nobody declared.
G3_denominators.DEN_A: SCENARIO-LEVEL, advancement-relevant. DEN_A = { r in holdout : r.clarificationExpected === true }. NUM_A = { r in DEN_A : provider raised a clarification on r }. recall_A = |NUM_A| / |DEN_A|. Eligible provenance classes: ALL THREE. A zero-candidate provider output on a DEN_A row IS A MISS, counted in the denominator and excluded from the numerator (section 40.2, D-58). A malformed record REMAINS in DEN_A and counts as a MISS; it is never dropped.
G3_denominators.DEN_B: CANDIDATE-CONDITIONED, diagnostic but still hard-gated. DEN_B = { r in DEN_A : provider emitted at least one candidate on r }. NUM_B = { r in DEN_B : provider raised a clarification on r }. recall_B = |NUM_B| / |DEN_B|. Same eligible provenance classes. A zero-candidate row is EXCLUDED from DEN_B -- that exclusion is the metric's definition. A malformed record is excluded from DEN_B iff it emitted no candidate; otherwise it remains and counts as a MISS.
G3_denominators.bindingRules: G3 passes ONLY if recall_A === 1.0 AND recall_B === 1.0. Both are hard gates (P-09R C, D-84). Neither substitutes for the other and they are NEVER merged into one number (D-58). Cardinalities are computed at scoring time from frozen truth metadata and were deliberately not computed at amendment time. |DEN_A| = 0 is a CONSTRUCTION FAILURE, not a pass -- the builder MUST THROW; D-D guarantees a non-empty floor of 6. No row may be added to, removed from, or reclassified between these denominators after any provider output has been observed (D-72, D-84).
G3_denominators.thresholdUnchanged: 100% on both. NOT CHANGED BY THIS AMENDMENT.

families.F3: insufficient evidence | n=3 | observation names a hazard-bearing condition but the decision-critical fact is EXPLICITLY not observable | conditionState INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE | ACTIVE prohibited YES | clarification REQUIRED | pole CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED | G3 YES | G7 no | G4 YES

D_D_authoredControls.derivedGateMemberships: G3 (CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED) from authored rows: EXACTLY 6 (F3 3 + F6 3) -- guarantees |DEN_A| >= 6 so G3 can never pass vacuously. G7 (CLARIFICATION_MUST_NOT_ASK) pole: EXACTLY 11 (F1 4 + F2 4 + F7 3). G4 (false ACTIVE) denominator: EXACTLY 18 (F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F8b).
D_D_authoredControls.G7_governance: G7 MEMBERSHIP IS A PROPERTY OF THE FAMILY SPECIFICATION AND IS NEVER SELF-AUTHORED AFTER INFERENCE. L3-INV-06 permits a question ONLY at a decision boundary; a family is intrinsically CLARIFICATION_MUST_NOT_ASK IFF its construction rule guarantees no boundary exists. F1 (condition explicitly negated), F2 (remediation explicitly completed -- precedent C-CS-05) and F7 (hazard and every decision-critical fact explicitly present -- precedent F-CL-04) qualify. F4, F5 and F8 are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: section 49.3 holds that expectClarification: false is NOT the same as MUST-NOT-ASK -- on a non-MUST_NOT_ASK pole it means 'this scenario does not require a question', on the pole it means 'a question here is a regression'. Conflating them is the D-58 error that D-76 found still live in the precision metric; this amendment does not repeat it. NO INDEPENDENT_GAUNTLET OR INDEPENDENT_REALISM ROW MAY EVER CARRY THE MUST_NOT_ASK POLE -- that would require judging semantically that a regulator record contains every decision-critical fact. G7's pole is composed EXCLUSIVELY of the 11 authored rows.
D_D_authoredControls.independenceOfAuthoring: PROTECTED. Controls are authored from the D-D.3 family specifications ALONE. The selected positive stride MUST NOT be read, previewed or semantically inspected before or during authoring, and controls are NOT derived by taking a selected acceptance row and modifying it. No control may be added, removed, retitled, re-allocated or re-poled in response to any provider output. Truth labels are fixed before the model sees any row. Authoring may draw on the already-open, already-spent L3-2b..L3-2f development material for SHAPE, since it is retired for gate use.
D_D_authoredControls.evidenceAuthorityBehavior: F3 and F6 must be resolvable ONLY by a question, never by asserting an unobserved fact: a row asserting ACTIVE on either is a G4 false-ACTIVE AND a G3 recall miss. F1, F2 and F8b must not have their negation recovered into an active hazard. No control may induce a NON_RETRYABLE_VALIDATION_REASONS code; any such code on an authored row is a G6 failure and is reported, never suppressed.
D_D_authoredControls.provenanceMarking: Every holdout row carries: provenanceClass (INDEPENDENT_GAUNTLET | INDEPENDENT_REALISM | AUTHORED_CONTROL); source (filename AND frozen sha256, or the authored-by string); sourceId (frozen scenarioId/id, or AC-<family>-<nn>); selectionRule (e.g. 'gauntlet.source.v1 - CMP(scenarioId) asc - i % 4 === 0'); pole; family (F1..F8 for authored rows, null otherwise). The by-provenance table (section 36.5) is MANDATORY and every gated metric is reported both overall AND split by provenanceClass. Authored rows supplement and never constitute the independent evidence.
D_D_authoredControls.duplicateOverlapRule: Comparison key is NORM(carrier). The builder MUST THROW -- never skip, never de-duplicate silently, never replace -- on collision with: (1) any observation in gauntlet.source.v1 (all 150, not merely the selected 38); (2) any in field-realism-pack-v2 (all 117); (3) any in gauntlet.seed (all 100, the reserve tranche); (4) any other authored control; (5) any row of the six prior sealed holdouts holdout-l32{,b,c,d,e,f}.json; (6) any row of every development set including the l32d and l32f devsets; (7) any row of the exhausted field corpus safescope-field-validation-dataset.v1.json; (8) any observation from a previously spent acceptance offset of either source. Additionally THROW if any two rows within the assembled 92-row holdout share NORM(carrier) or share a sourceId. gauntlet.seed is CHECKED but NOT DRAWN FROM; it carries one internal duplicate text pair and a future amendment opening it must state its duplicate policy.

run1State.whyAllThreeCoexist: They answer THREE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. The literal output is a fact about a PROGRAM (what did this deterministic function return on these inputs). The governed terminal is a fact about a RUN (what does the programme record as its outcome, supplying the classification the scorer's vocabulary could not express). The model result is a fact about a MODEL (what has been measured). ONLY THE THIRD COULD EVER ADVANCE OR BLOCK L3-3, AND IT IS EMPTY. The governed terminal does not overrule the scorer's arithmetic; it states the conditions under which that arithmetic is meaningful, and those conditions were not met.

rootCauseOfScorabilityDefect.proximateCause: The frozen scorer's ENTIRE invalidity vocabulary -- MALFORMED_RESULT_RECORD, MISSING_RESULTS, EXTRA_RESULTS, DUPLICATE_RESULTS, DEN_A_EMPTY -- asks only RESULT-SET-SHAPE questions. All five were zero on Run 1, so invalid=[] and scorable=true.
rootCauseOfScorabilityDefect.underlyingCause: REPRESENTATIONAL, NOT ARITHMETIC. Every field of the frozen nine-field result-record contract encodes 'not evaluated' IN BAND, using a value a genuinely evaluated row could also produce: schemaValid=false, retries=0, candidates=[], raisedClarification=false, assertedState=null, empty code arrays, safetyConsequentialRejection=false. THE SCORER CANNOT DISTINGUISH 'THE MODEL ANSWERED AND ASSERTED NOTHING' FROM 'THE MODEL WAS NEVER ASKED'.

contaminationRunsBothDirections.fabricatedFailure: G1, G3 and G10 count a non-evaluated row as a substantive MISS. Run 1: G3 counted 27 unevaluated DEN_A rows as recall misses -> 1/29. G10 -> 40/92.
contaminationRunsBothDirections.denominatorCollapse: G2's denominator is result-dependent; a non-evaluated row silently LEAVES it. Run 1: collapsed to 2 raised rows.
contaminationRunsBothDirections.fabricatedPass: G4, G5, G6, G7, G8 cannot be tripped by a non-evaluated row. Run 1: G4 0-of-21 and G7 0-of-11 PASSED WITH ZERO OF THEIR DENOMINATORS EVALUATED.
contaminationRunsBothDirections.g9FailsBothWaysAtOnce: 52 rows unevaluated in BOTH processes COMPARED EQUAL and scored REPRODUCIBLE -- agreeing about nothing. 40 rows evaluated on one side only scored DIVERGENT -- disagreeing about nothing.

rootCauseOfScorabilityDefect.conclusion: THE REPAIR IS NOT A GATE CHANGE. It is a PRE-SCORING VALIDITY GATE. No threshold moves, no denominator moves, no arithmetic changes.

disclosuresRecordedRatherThanConcealed.scoreArtifactTimestamp: PROCEDURAL ERROR, DISCLOSED: the package was manifested and the scorer was THEN re-run as a final re-verification, which rewrote ACCEPTANCE_SCORE.json with a fresh scoredAt and broke the manifest. THE VERDICT DID NOT CHANGE -- only the clock did. Rather than quietly re-manifest, a determinism proof was added (scoring/prove-score-determinism.js) showing the scorer is a pure function of (holdout, resultsA, resultsB) and that the SCORE_BODY_DIGEST is stable. A first revision of THAT proof was itself defective -- it excluded only scoredAt and so reported "THE VERDICT MOVED" when the invocation path string changed between a repo-relative and an absolute call; it was corrected to exclude both environment-dependent fields and to assert the raw-evidence CONTENT digests instead. THREE INSTRUMENT DEFECTS HAVE NOW BEEN FOUND AND CORRECTED IN THIS PROGRAMME BY THE SAME PATTERN: a check that measured its own source text or its own invocation environment rather than the thing under test.

rootCauseOfObservedStalePricing.statement: The $6.99 Pro / $11.99 Expert pricing observed in the browser came from corrupted/stale .next build output, not from the working tree. A next build / next start process overwrote frontend-next/.next while next dev was running on :3000 and serving from the same directory, so the dev server served stale/broken output from that directory.
measured: next dev on :3000 answered HTTP 500 on /register and /pricing.
An isolated next dev started on :3002 from the SAME working tree answered 200 on /register, /pricing, /upgrade and /settings.
Those isolated renders carried exactly one decimal price, $24.99, with Expert x0, 6.99 x0, 11.99 x0.
next start on :3001 also served $24.99 with no Expert.
No customer-facing source file in the repository contains 6.99 or 11.99.
git log -S places both strings entirely before 2026-08-17: 8d91109b removed Expert, 9ff13757 moved Pro to $9.99.
frontend-next/.next build artifacts were dated AFTER the :3000 dev server's start time.
rootCauseOfObservedStalePricing.inference: The 500 on :3000 is MEASURED and is fully explained by the .next collision. That the specific $6.99/$11.99 strings were served from that same corrupted/cached output is INFERRED, not captured: the reporting browser's response was not recorded. What is established either way is that current source has not contained those prices since 2026-08-17.
rootCauseOfObservedStalePricing.remedy: Restart next dev. Never run next build against the same .next/ directory while a dev server is using it.
rootCauseOfObservedStalePricing.structuralRootCause: Every customer-facing price is an authored string literal in the component that renders it -- app/register/page.tsx, components/pricing/PricingContent.tsx (which also backs /upgrade) and lib/planEntitlements.ts#getPlanPricing() each carried their own copy. Nothing derived one from another and nothing asserted they agreed, so every reprice was a three-file memory exercise and registration is the one that kept being missed.

scopeDecision.converted: /field-capture — a NEW small route that is durable offline
scopeDecision.why: The workspace is the guided HazLenz flow (analysis, evidence, risk, findings, corrective actions, report). All of it is server-authoritative and entitlement-gated, and it creates the server record before the first step. Making it offline-tolerant would have required either copying governed analysis onto the device or letting a local substitute stand in for it. What a field inspector actually loses without signal is the ability to RECORD what they see, which is what this phase makes durable.

localUserIsolation.namespace: userKey = 'u_' + SHA-256('insite-offline-v1:' + <account id>), derived from the authenticated session
properties: part of EVERY primary key and the only index, so the store exposes no 'list everything' path
with no session resolveOfflineIdentity() returns null, which IS the boundary rather than a check layered over one
reads re-verify the namespace after decryption; a decrypted draft with a foreign userKey is discarded
reproducible for the same account and nobody else, so ordinary sign-out leaves a user's own drafts recoverable at their next sign-in without exposing them to whoever signs in between
localUserIsolation.encryptionAtRest: AES-GCM under a per-account key held in the same database.
localUserIsolation.encryptionThreatModelStatedHonestly: The key is on the device, so this is NOT protection against an attacker who controls the device or can run the application's own code. It buys that payloads are not legible plaintext in a storage inspector, and that 'remove offline data from this device' destroys the key with the rows. The isolation guarantee the product depends on comes from the NAMESPACE, not from the encryption.
localUserIsolation.preExistingLeakClosed: lib/inspection/offlineInspectionStore.ts (legacy /inspection route) writes insite_offline_inspections_v1, insite_offline_report_drafts_v1, insite_offline_inspection_sync_queue_v1 and insite_active_local_inspection_id to DEVICE-GLOBAL localStorage with no account namespace — raw observation text, local findings and report drafts, surviving sign-out. Same class as V1-LOCALISO-01. All four keys are now in clearAuthSession()'s sweep.
localUserIsolation.logoutBehavior: Ordinary sign-out makes the prior account's local content unreachable (no session -> no namespace -> no query). The data remains recoverable ONLY by the same authenticated account. An explicit 'remove this account's offline data from this device' control destroys that account's drafts, photos and key material and touches no other account.

synchronization.model: Explicit, user-initiated, APPEND-ONLY. A button, not a background process.
synchronization.serverHasNoIdempotencyKey: CreateInspectionDto and CreateObservationDto accept no client-supplied key, and adding one is a schema change to the protected development database, which this phase is not authorised to make.
synchronization.duplicatePrevention: Claim-and-reconcile on the client: a syncAttempt marker is persisted BEFORE the create; a retry that finds the marker with no recorded identifier first looks for the record the interrupted attempt may already have created and ADOPTS it. Adoption requires a UNIQUE match on title, site and a timestamp at or after the attempt started, excluding any remote id another local draft already claims. Two plausible candidates refuse adoption rather than guess.
synchronization.acknowledgementRule: Every identifier the server returns is written to IndexedDB immediately, one at a time. An already-acknowledged observation is skipped on retry. SYNCED is set ONLY when every part was acknowledged; anything outstanding leaves the draft SYNC_FAILED with the local copy intact.
synchronization.noHazLenz: Synchronising capture does not run analysis. Analysis stays on the existing online, entitlement-gated path.

conflictHandling.structuralGuarantee: Synchronisation issues no PATCH, no DELETE and no status transition against server-held records, so silent destructive overwrite is structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely.
conflictHandling.stalenessCheck: A draft attached to a server inspection records the version it last reconciled against. If the server advanced past it, or the inspection was archived, the draft goes to CONFLICT BEFORE anything is appended.
userChoice: Keep both — detaches the draft so the next sync creates a SEPARATE inspection; the server copy is untouched
Keep the server copy — marks the local draft resolved so it can be removed
conflictHandling.whyPartial: Detection and a user choice are implemented and proven. Automatic merging does not exist and was not built. PARTIAL is the honest label: what is proven is that newer server data is never silently overwritten and the user is given the decision.

autoRetriedNonIdempotentCreate.defect: apiFetch retries once when a request THROWS (timeout or lost connection). For a create carrying no idempotency key that is a duplicate factory: the server commits the row, the response is lost, and the automatic retry creates a second one before any client code can observe the failure.
autoRetriedNonIdempotentCreate.measured: The browser suite lets POST /inspections reach the server and then destroys the response. Before the fix, ONE interrupted sync produced TWO server inspections, and the deliberately conservative adopt-only-when-unique rule then refused to adopt either, so the retry created a third.
autoRetriedNonIdempotentCreate.fix: lib/canonicalWorkflowApi.ts — createPersistedSite, createPersistedInspection, addPersistedObservation and uploadInspectionEvidence are marked NON_IDEMPOTENT (retries: 0).
autoRetriedNonIdempotentCreate.preExisting: This was a latent defect on the ONLINE path too: the same double-create was reachable from /inspections 'Start inspection' on a flaky connection. Offline capture did not introduce it; it made it observable.

offlineFallbackDefect.defect: An /offline App Router page used as the service worker's navigation fallback looked correct and was not. A cached Next document is inert only until it hydrates; the App Router then reconciles against the CURRENT URL, and the offline message was replaced in the browser by that URL's client render or by Next's 404.
offlineFallbackDefect.measured: An offline navigation to an unknown path rendered '404 — This page could not be found'; one to /settings rendered Settings. Neither was the fallback that had actually been served.
offlineFallbackDefect.fix: public/offline.html — a plain static document, no hydration, no external stylesheet, script, font or image. app/offline/ was removed.

harnessCorrections.serviceWorkerOfflineEmulation: context.setOffline(true) alone was NOT sufficient to prove offline reopening. It severs page-originated requests reliably, but after a persistent context is closed and reopened the SERVICE-WORKER target does not pick the emulation up, so the worker's own fetch() still reached the server. With setOffline() alone, a reopened session's navigation to an unknown path returned the live Next.js 404 FROM THE SERVER — an assertion that would have passed without the network ever being down. The suite now also aborts at the route layer, which does cover service-worker requests (verified: 14 intercepted requests on a reopened session), and asserts the offline fallback as its own check that the emulation is in force.
harnessCorrections.devAuthBypass: backend/.env sets DEV_AUTH_BYPASS=true. With the bypass on, an unauthenticated request is answered as a synthetic user, and the two 'unauthenticated must be 401' probes in test:cross-user-isolation fail. Run the disposable API with DEV_AUTH_BYPASS=false. Harness setting, not a product defect.
harnessCorrections.authRateLimit: POST /auth/login is throttled to 5 per 60s per IP. The offline suite switches accounts repeatedly because that IS the isolation test, so it waits the window out rather than reporting a rate limit as an authorisation defect — the same effect section 79.10 recorded. Run the backend auth suites with a similar gap between them.
harnessCorrections.serviceWorkerNotInDev: The worker is deliberately not registered under next dev; a cached shell in front of a rebuilding dev server serves stale chunks. The offline suite therefore needs a production build.

whyTheSection80MechanismWasReplaced.previousMechanism: Client-side claim-and-reconcile: a syncAttempt marker persisted before a create, and on retry a search for the record that attempt might already have made, matched on title + site + timestamp.
whyTheSection80MechanismWasReplaced.defect1: It is a similarity judgement, not identity. Two legitimate inspections created minutes apart at the same site with the same title are indistinguishable to it. Section 80 handled that by adopting only on a UNIQUE match, which turns a repeat-visit site — the ordinary case in field safety work — into one where recovery deadlocks and retrying cannot fix a SYNC_FAILED draft.
whyTheSection80MechanismWasReplaced.defect2: Even a single match is a guess. Nothing established that the candidate was the record the interrupted attempt created rather than a similar one that already existed.

identityContract.mechanism: The client mints a stable opaque clientRequestId, persists it with the local record, and replays it unchanged on every attempt. The DATABASE is the authority that one identifier means one row.
identityContract.identityValue: The offline store's existing localId — already stable across refresh, restart and sign-out — so no new concept was introduced on the device, only a new use for one that was already durable.
identityContract.format: [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{8,128}. Bounded and character-restricted so it can never carry structure the server might interpret. It is an identity, never an authorisation input.
identityContract.scoping: Per CREATING USER, never per organisation. Authorised organisation sharing governs who may READ an inspection; it does not govern whose WRITE a request is. Keying on createdByUserId means one member of an organisation can never resolve or adopt a colleague's record by presenting their identifier — deliberately stricter than the read model.
identityContract.sitesExcluded: Sites are resolved by NAME and were deliberately left alone. A site's name is already its user-facing identity (the existing Saved site picker selects by it) and the server holds a uniqueness constraint on it, so a create whose response was lost is recovered by the lookup the sync runs first anyway.

concurrency.problem: A check-then-insert is not a lock: two concurrent replays both miss the check and both insert.
concurrency.resolution: The partial unique index rejects the loser. For an idempotent create that rejection is the CORRECT outcome, not an error: the loser catches SQLSTATE 23505, re-reads, and returns what won. src/common/unique-violation.ts checks both the TypeORM wrapper's code and the nested driverError.code, because the shape differs between driver versions.
concurrency.measured: Ten concurrent replays of one inspection identifier resolve to one row with no error surfaced to any caller; eight concurrent replays of an observation identifier likewise.

evidenceUploads.readyOnly: Only a READY stored object satisfies a replay. An uploading or failed row is an attempt whose bytes may never have reached the provider, so it is RE-DRIVEN on the same row rather than duplicated — a half-written upload is never reported as stored.
evidenceUploads.selectFalseHazard: objectKey is select:false, so a record re-read by identifier does not carry it. Finalisation reloads the key explicitly and updates status BY ID rather than save()-ing a partially-loaded entity. Recorded because it would otherwise have been a silent corruption.

deleted: the syncAttempt marker it depended on
heuristicRemoved.assertedAbsent: check:offline-field-capture asserts that no candidate matching and no ambiguity resolution survives in the sync path, so it cannot return.
heuristicRemoved.conflictDetachConsequence: 'Keep both' detaches a draft so the next sync creates a SEPARATE inspection — but clientRequestId is exactly what the server resolves to the inspection being left, so replaying it would return that same inspection. Detaching therefore re-mints EVERY server-facing identity the draft holds (the inspection's, every observation's and every photo's) and clears each acknowledgement with it.

backwardCompatibility.oldClientNewServer: No identifier is sent, no lookup runs, no index applies (all three are partial on IS NOT NULL). Asserted directly: two identifier-less creates produce two independent inspections, and an identifier-less evidence upload still works.
backwardCompatibility.newClientOldServer: The only caller that sends an identifier is offline sync — a feature nobody can be mid-flight on during the deploy, since /inspections 'Start inspection' sends none. In the parallel-deploy window the worst case is a first-minute offline sync answering 400 (the ValidationPipe runs forbidNonWhitelisted), surfacing as SYNC_FAILED with the draft intact and retryable. Stated rather than discovered.

operatorError.whatHappened: The FIRST production migration attempt failed with 'cannot execute ALTER TABLE in a read-only transaction'.
operatorError.cause: The read-only preflight had run SET SESSION CHARACTERISTICS AS TRANSACTION READ ONLY through Neon's POOLER endpoint. In transaction pooling that setting persists on the pooled SERVER connection and is inherited by whichever client next reuses that backend. Established rather than guessed: pg_db_role_setting was empty and pg_settings.source read 'session', which is what distinguishes a leaked session default from a persistent configuration change.
operatorError.dataImpact: NONE. The migration aborted before its first statement; migrations still read 46 and no clientRequestId column existed.
operatorError.remediation: Cleared deliberately rather than waited out — SET SESSION CHARACTERISTICS AS TRANSACTION READ WRITE across the pool, then twelve fresh pooled connections re-checked at 'off', plus a rolled-back write probe. This mattered because the running API connects through that same pooler and a poisoned backend would have failed real customer writes.
operatorError.thenApplied: Over the DIRECT (non-pooled) endpoint, which is the correct channel for DDL regardless.
operatorError.lesson: Do not run a read-only preflight through a connection pooler.
